May, 1997  No.117   Page Reply

 Sam Quigg............03    06

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

Sam Quigg, LIMAVADY, N. IRELAND



Dear Ron & Brian,

I have two separate models of
INTERFACE 1.  According to the
Microdrive formatting program
INCREMAT, one has an old rom and
the other has a new ROM. Can you
please enlighten me as to the
differences in the ROMS?

I believe there are different
models of MULTIFACE 128. I have
one, albeit quite elderly judg-
ing by the instruction leaflet,
which doesn't seem to like being
in the same company as a DATEL
+D interface.

ROMANTIC ROBOT, who are still
marketing the 128 version of the
Multiface say in their literat-
ure that it is compatible with
the +D. Any ideas??


I have obtained a copy of THE
LAST WORD wordprocessing program
on tape.  It is version 2.1 and
is complete with code patches
for, several disk systems, but,
alas, none for the+D.  Are you
familiar with this word process-
ing program and how I might con-
vert it, or perhaps some other
OUTLET reader might have the
know-how. I would appreciate any
assistance with this project.


I'm trying to get WRITER 48K to
print to an Epson FX-80 fitted
with a serial interface, from a
128K Spectrum via the RS 232
port without success.There isn't
any suitable interface listed in
the Writer program. Any ideas?

I would be grateful for any help
with the above problems.

                Regards,


                Sam  Quigg

Brian Cavers to Sam Quigg

Spectrum's fitted with Interface
1 shadow ROM Issue 2 will print
80 (after a reset) if you enter:

        PRINT PEEK 23729

In Issue 2, the "t" channel out-
put has been improved to support
the TAB function and the comma
control code (code 6 which tabs
to column 16 then to the start
of the next line). The leading
space bug in Issue 1 has also
been corrected.

There is the new system variable
at 23729 mentioned above which
you can POKE to alter line width
when printing. (default is 80)

The CAT command and other 'read'
routines should be faster in the
Issue 2 because it doesn't waste
time trying to read non-existent
sectors.

One VERY important change is the
memory check when accessing the
drive. I used an Issue 1 Inter-
face 1 while Ron had an Issue 2.
As I recall, if there was less
than around 700 bytes of memory
free then the whole system would
lock up and you had to reset. It
drove me crazy at times, especi-
ally if I had just spent half an
hour writing a program and then
it locked up when I went to SAVE
it! This problem alone makes it
well worth using an Issue 2!


A 'carriage return' (code 13)
to start a new line is NOT sent
when the "b" channel is CLOSEd
with Issue 2 but was with Issue
1.

If BREAK was pressed during a
CLOSE operation then it became
impossible to remove the channel
(from BASIC) with Issue 1. This
bug has been corrected in Issue
2.

There are two new hook codes in
Issue 2 for machine code progr-
ammers but these don't affect
BASIC. I have details if you
want though.



Checks made by the FORMAT comm-
and are direct OUT instructions
in Issue 2 rather than using a
channel - though I can't see it
making any visible difference to
the user.

There are other changes which,
like the preceding, are probably
not visible to the user but are
simply more efficient routines
used by the system etc.

I have fuller details should you
need to know more about any of
the differences. These are taken
from the book, "Spectrum Shadow
ROM Disassembly" by Gianluca
Carri which you might spot at a
Microfair if you are lucky!


Possibly your Multiface 128 is
an earlier version that is not
compatible with the +D. The only
128K Spectrum I have is the +3
but I do have the Lunter Z80
emulator on the PC. This can
emulate a 128K Spectrum with +D
and Multiface 128. I tried this
and it successfully saved and
reloaded a snapshot so clearly
this version of Multiface IS
compatible with the +D.

When you say, 'not compatible'
do you mean the whole Spectrum
crashes if both your Multiface
and +D are connected - or that
the Multiface will not operate?
If, in fact, it does run and you
can get the yellow menu bar at
the bottom of the screen then...

If you select SAVE and enter a
filename do you get options for
tape, microdrive, Disciple and
Opus? If you can get that far
but there is no Disciple or +D
option then I would say your
particular Multiface is not
compatible and may have been
made even before the Disciple
was launched.

However, if not compatible you
might also get a hardware clash
just by having the Multiface and
+D connected to the Spectrum at
the same time. If this happens
then it's worth at least clean-
ing the edge connector (switch
off the power first!) just in
case it simply a bad connection.


Short of buying a new Multiface
I don't see what else you can do
however, I do wonder what use a
Multiface snapshot is on a +D
when it has its own snapshot
built in.

While testing a made a Multiface
snapshot from the emulator on
this current OUTLET disk of the
HEAD OVER HEELS 128K game (on
the +D version only). This can
be loaded from BASIC with...

 LOAD d*"HOHmf128" or LOAD P40

However, I am not sure what that
will prove because I found it
would reload into the emulator
WITHOUT Multiface! Is that supp-
osed to happen I wonder!

I know of THE LAST WORD but have
not seen it I don't think. In
OUTLET 42 there is an OUTLETTER
from Andy Fleming who indicates
he has it running on his +D. If
you see this Andy, please write
in and confirm!  I believe that
Malcolm Perry has TLW too though
uses OUTWRITE now on the SAM. If
anyone else has any info on this
please let us know or contact
Sam Quigg direct (see his advert
in OUTBOARD).

I could find nothing about conv-
erting THE WRITER to print via
the Spectrum 128K RS232 port but
R.A. Roberts reported in OUTLET
71 that he had been helped by
someone who got it working on a
+D. Would that help?

If anyone else has any ideas on
any of the subjects in this let-
ter then please write!

                        Brian

From: Colin Bibby, MANCHESTER

Dear All,

Sadness comes to mind here if my
BAEC (British Amateur Electonics
Club)membership ceases.Likewise,
if OUTLET closes its doors to +3
users.

The BAEC has been in operation
for over thirty years now but is
apparently hitting a rocky patch
of late largely due to secretar-
ial problems. It seems that one
Mr. Perfect (don't know who) has
had the gall to condemn Alf (the
secretary) for spellings. There-
fore, old Alf has decided to
stand down from office leaving
the BAEC minus a secretary.

I understand the original found-
er of the BAEC, Herbert, who is
now over 80 years of age,is back
at the helm almost single-hand-
edly - although not for long I
fear if they don't find a secr-
etary soon surely - which makes
me wish I was clever enough to
take it all on, but I ain't.


My YTC venture is a far simpler
(safer) alternative for myself
and a number of personal friends
who enjoy electronics for fun
other than as a profession
thereby eliminating much of the
physics involved. Electrons for
fun can also be balanced.



Now I hear that the fab 'OUTLET'
might close its doors to the +3
users - surely not OUTLET too!
The +D might be all well and
good for those lucky enough to
own one but the MF3 doesn't work
well with Disccrip, therefore
other problems must also exist
surely with the +D.


I have been working hard on my
YTC project since arrival of the
last quarterly BAEC newsletter
in January this year believing
all was going well but [the
prospect of] no OUTLET certainly
puts obstacles in my way.



Regarding your questionnaire,you
missed the 4th and 5th options..
Hard copy and tape versions (ob-
viously not applicable)

I understand that the +D was for
5.25" floppy disks and therefore
should function equally well
using HD/DD 3.5". No particular
+D advantage here as far as I
can see over the +3 unless it is
that the +D is more common. What
are the advantages of the +D?

Oh no, never mind. It is plainly
obvious that many +D users do
exist therefore will also need
some much consideration as far
as OUTLET is concerned.


5.25 floppy disks will soon dry
up; so too will 3.5" DD disks. I
understand the production of DD
drives have now ceased worldwide
in favour of the later HD. Yet
these 1.44mb drives are soon to
follow the same route in favour
of later 2mb and gigabyte types?

In the light of all this I have
already stocked myself with 3.5"
DD drives and DD disks. The +3
is very happy indeed having a DD
drive plugged into its backside
turning it into a twin drive and
extremely versatile M+system. My
excess stocks are intended to
keep me going for the remainder
of my days which might amount to
around a further 30/40 years of
life left in this old dog yet.

I can't be doing with all that
constant updating and expanding
of the modern world every five
minutes. Seems idiotic to me
while it obviously suits many
users to be used.


So, for me personally it's the
DD 720K (710K ZX) format of pre-
ference for my OUTLET disk which
seems unlikely at present. How-
ever, shopping aorund at the
rallies can uncover these used
DD drives at prices around a
tenner although as a used drive,
well need I say more - It's a
risk.



My recently acquired additional
DD drives stock were picked up
on my behalf by pensioner friend
fellow ZXer and BAEC member Eric
from the rally in Blackpool on
March 97. Of the ten drives five
were faulty and will be returned
for either refund or exchange
(my choice). The IBM dealer pre-
sently supplying me has a stock
of these drives which aren't of
any further use to IBMers which
suits me fine at just `6 each
although as stated some further
inconvenience is involved plus
Eric's [fuel] tank and entrance
fees with each run are also my
bill to cover but helps me to
feel more secure with my needs,
etc.


The 3.5" advantage is tremendous
and varied when considering the
+3 which ought to be of further
interest. However, the kit...

Problems arise with pricing the
complete DD drive for the +3.
Maplin stock parts for data
carrier ribbon cable plus +3
"B:" drive edge connector and
data bus DIL plug for rear of DD
comes to around `3+, etc. The
5v/12v power supply lead comes
to about the same price and does
not include the PSU to drive it.

I have arranged for pensioner
friend Bill to transport me to
the next rally for return of
those faulty drives.


Most of my 3.5" disks have that
ADMIN saved since the 710K form-
at often exceeds 64 files.

  COPY "A:FILENAME; TO "B:" :

  COPY "A:"*.*" TO "B:", etc

        ...and vice versa do all
work well.


My thanks to Malcolm Goodman who
answered my request for informa-
tion with regard to the ATY
Specmate interface apparently
from around 1985/6 after the
Multiface had hit the scene.



It would please me to discover
how to POKE back into the Spec-
trum font. A nice quantity of ZX
came into my possession some
time ago including Datel mouse,
MF3 and Digi digitiser. Many
discs are of OUTLET and included
fonts but little detail of the
ZX font was found. The manual
doesn't seem to mention the ZX
font POKE either or maybe I'm
looking too hard.

Best wishes to all at OUTLET.

                   Colin

Brian Cavers to Colin Bibby



Thanks for all the info about B:
drives, etc, Colin. Hopefully we
can sort something out for the
+3.

As far as a tape version, we no
longer produce an OUTLET that
runs from tape as we used to but
you've got me wondering if the
+3 version might be produced on
tape with an auto-transfer to +3
disk. It should be possible but
might be awkward and impractical
for us. However, I will have a
word with Ron. Hard copy of just
OUTLET text? Same answer!


The Disciple and +D was always
workable with either 3.5" or
5.25" disks and most people used
3.5". We STILL DO produce
a 5.25" version of OUTLET but it is only for a handful of read-
ers .

The +D is faster, has more capa-
city and provides reading and
writing direct to files from the
BASIC as well as direct editing
of disk sectors- and, of course,
it includes a snapshot feature
as standard. I guess the main
advantage is disk capacity but a
+3 with a 3.5" B drive overcomes
that. I wonder if a 3.5" drive
could be fitted as the A drive
on a +3??!!

Query: will a standard +3 PSU be
OK to power a B drive? I think
so and suspect we may have had
this raised in OUTLET before but
you or someone might confirm.

To restore the normal Spectrum
font (character set) after a new
on has been displayed, use...

         POKE 23670,0
         POKE 23671,60

The rule is to POKE the address
(usual two-byte format) of the
font minus 256 and the standard
font is in ROM at 60 * 256 + 0
which is 15616

                       Brian

Brian Cavers to Ron Webster

To connect a +D to a +3 or +2A
Spectrum buy a "FIXIT" off Brian
Gaff (see later).

I am puzzled as to why you want
TWO emulators but presumably a
friend wants one too! Anyway,you
can order them from Brian Gaff
too (see later)

You are correct that the PC
floppy drive will let you access
your +D disks. This is a true
emulation (though a bit slow)
and means that you simply use
EXACTLY THE SAME SYNTAX to load
programs, eg, LOAD d1"name". It
is exactly as if you had a Spec-
trum with a +D attached!

Your disks may not be damaged.If
you got a "No system file" error
it just means there is no system
file on that particular disk and
you were entering "RUN" in a
blank Spectrum which, with a +D,
tries to first load the system
file and then a BASIC program
named "AUTO" followed by any six
characters you like.

This is how you would normally
use the +D.

1.Switch on the Spectrum or load
  the emulator if using a PC.

2.Put a disk in the drive with a
  system file on it. This file
  is named "+SYS" plus any six
  characters.

3. If the disk also has a BASIC
   program named "AUTO" plus any
   other six characters then it
   will also load and run but if
   not you just get an "OK".

4. There is no further need to
   load the system file ever
   again - even if you reset -
   unless (a) you switch off the
   machine and on again or...
   (b) the system gets corrupted
   (this sometimes happens with
   odd programs and you start
   getting odd disk errors).

5. Therefore, there is no need
   to have a system file on any
   other disk except one master
   and one or two backups disks.


6. To load further programs you
   use LOAD d1 "name" or LOAD Pn
   where "n" is the number shown
   in the CAT list. HOWEVER...

7. Some people PREFER to put the
   system file on all disks so
   they can then just enter RUN
   to load an AUTO file. I see
   little advantage in this as
   it is slower (because it has
   to keep loading TWO files!).
   I just always save my AUTO
   file as the first file on the
   disk and then I know I can
   always just enter LOAD P1. It
   is up to individual taste.

[On the SAM Coupe, if you reset
then you HAVE to reload the sys-
tem file but not with the +D]

I would like to congratulate
Bernadetta Dowsland for obtain-
ing an Opus Discovery but disa-
gree that it is primitive. For
those readers who have never
seen one,an Opus is a black box
containing up to two 3.5" disk
drives and power supply for them
and the ability to power the Sp-
ectrum as well through the edge
connector. On the left hand side
of the housing is a duplicate
edge connector for adding other
peripherals, a printer port for
connecting to a Centronics prin-
ter and a Kempston-type joystick
interface which can be turned on
and off from the BASIC.

The Opus is not as fast as the
+D though this can be cured by
purchasing a new ROM. There are
programs available to allow the
Opus to read +D disks and IBM-PC
720K format disks.

There is a user group for Opus
owners:-

[NOTE: I understand that this
club has recently ended - Brian]

The Spectrum Discovery Club(SDC)

       76 Mannville Road
    Keighley, West Yorkshire

Please include an SAE if writ-
ing.

the 'prize behind the three
doors' puzzle.  The same problem
was described on Radio 4's 'The
Afternoon Shift' with Laurie
Taylor.  But as is so often the
case the expert failed to expl-
ain the answer properly due to
time constraints. I find that
alot of these science programs
do the same, trying to cram too

Regarding the NASA ballpoint pen
(Outlet 115) that was specially
developed for use in zero grav-
ity whilst the Russians used a
pencil, I understand there is
some logic behind NASA's invent-
ion.Since a pencil lead consists

tricity. Now in zero gravity,wri

ound your spaceship full of vit-
al electrical equipment which
could be shorted out. So I know
which spaceship I would rather
be on! As an interesting aside,
Apple Computers put a warning in

sumably for similar reasons.

ors allow Opus Discovery disks

Brian Cavers to Ronald Raaijen

There is no need to reset your
PC before using the emulator. If
you use DISK720.COM from OUTLET
24 (PC version) in a BAT file
just before it loads the emulat-
ar you can then forget about the
problem! An alternative is just
to put a 720K DOS disk in Drive
A and DIR it before running the
emulator - but my program is far
easier!

The CAT and filename selection
part of TRANSTAPE is done in
BASIC whereas the actual copy-
ing to tape is done by machine
code in screen memory thus it
leaves all other Spectrum RAM
free for files being copied.

It follows that once you have
made your selections for copying
that the BASIC part of TRANSTAPE
is overwritten by whatever files
are being copied and is there-
fore no longer present when you
return to BASIC. However, with
the emulator, it is an extremely
easy and quick matter to simply
snapshot TRANSTAPE at the moment
the CAT screen first appears so
it can be recalled, ready to CAT
again, just by pressing F10, L
and ENTER!

I have written a program to stop
the printing of filenames on the
screen when loading from tape or
a tapefile in the emulator so it
makes running the TAP OUTLET so
much neater!....

The software is NOTAPRIN and is
in this month's OUTLET(PC only).
There are actually two programs;
one creates a modified version
of the emulator's ROM file and
the other is a BAT file used to
switch in the new ROM file and
run the emulator then restore
the original ROM.

I have just done it in a great
hurry following a sudden inspir-
ation but it seems to work very
well indeed! The TAP version of
OUTLET now loads very neatly. I
hope that helps.

                         Brian

From:Malcolm Perry,KIDDERMINSTER





Dear Ron and Brian.

During the recent CH5 test as
expected I received very little.
In this part of the Midlands the
main transmitter is at Sutton
Coldfield some 25 - 30 miles NE
(ish), Between it and us is the
hump of the Clent Hills and as

and Bewdley are all on rivers in

polarised and of the wrong group
it is little wonder all I got
was a whiff of a faint signal.
What was interesting though was
that a B&W portable received a
fair picture in the loft off its
own loop aerial. This shows that
with a proper aerial in the
right direction we should be OK.

In fact, before the repeaters,
BBC2 had to be taken from Sutton
and so a number of the older ae-
rials are in the right direction
but newer ones tend to be on lo-
cal transmitters.

The signal was strong enough to

strength as the other 4 from Su-
tton so I would guess it was on
normal power.I do not know about

TV but I do know the computers
generate that much hash that I

local transmitter.


The signal from CH5 would not be
strong enough to cause problems
even with a proper aerial but
the computers could cause probl-
ems to CH5. This however is not
so much from the modulator but
generated from the actual comp-
uter processor circuits.


From the info so far it would
seem my previous predictions in
a past Outlet that unless you
are actually close to the trans-
mitter, CH5 is unlikely to cause
problems to computers even if on
the same CH. with the computer
connected properly and directly
to the TV.


How much computers interfere
with CH5 is unpredictable but
again unlikely unless extremely
close to the TV or in extremely
weak signal areas. Video recor-
ders and satellite systems will
be the main retuning necessity
and most TV sets will need tun-
ing to CH5 on a "spare" button.

I recently read a comment where
it was stated that while exist-
ing recorders would be retuned,
many in the shops may not be.The
problem could go on for some
time when buying new.Makers are
also looking into now designing
recorders and satellite equip-
ment that can have the modulator
(the source of problems) turned
off and just use SCART links.

I foresee before too long the
modulator way of connecting to
TV sets will be obsolete on new
equipment and just SCART will be
used.It will also then free more
channels for CH5 to use(which at
the moment are seriously in
short supply) to allow better
coverage.

Digital TV is now also being
implemented and it is said into
the next century it will ALL be
digital. TV as we know it will
not exist. Just as UHF saw the
end of 405.

So digital TV with a few dozen
channels for each operator. sat-
ellite with all theirs, cable TV
- we will not have time to use


computers in any case so there
will not be any problem. The
whole nation will be locked in
their own individual rooms and
do their shopping,leisure, work,
and travel in virtual reality
round the world at will all from
the "interactive box in the cor-
ner" - if you believe everything
you read that is.

Talking of Cable TV,we have just
had the pleasure of the upheaval
of digging up the locality for
miles around and every road and
street to install it. We had the
notification they were going to
start in this road. A large hole
appeared near our house some 8ft
square and just as deep and ano-
ther a bit lower down.

We then had a notice the water
was going to be turned off. Out
of the large hole appeared a
length of cable that was taken
to a new cable TV junction box
on the side of the pavement. The
hole was filled in.The following
day two men in a water board van
and jackets opened up the cable
TV box and did some electrical
tests. They then moved to where
the next hole had been and did
the same in that new box. That
did raise the question as to
what water had to do with cable
TV?

Then along came the TV company
and put in all their cabling. I
can only presume the water board


are fitting some form of monit-
oring or metering in their main
supply pipes and use the cable
telephone links back to their
control room.

                Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry


I use a signal booster and just
about get a Channel 5 picture
that is watchable - but it is
very borderline and I have only
watched it a few times. In fact
there is so little on Channel 5
that interests me that I shall
only watch it if something extra
brilliant is on!

I have retuned my video provis-
ionally. There is a very slight

ered to try retuning it yet but

I do notice though, that some-
times there is distortion when a
car passes by. I think this may
be due to the fact that I am us-
ing a signal booster and because
the overlap of video output and
Channel 5 is very borderline, a
sudden reflection off a car
slightly improves the signal off
of Channel 5 and causes the ext-
ra distortion. I think that will
be resolved when I no longer
need the booster.


I also think that if one could
turn the aerial to point at the
transmitter that is sending CH 5
at the moment in this area AND
use a signal booster, then it
may make the picture quite fair.


It's a pity my signal booster
does not have a 'straight thru'
mode switch which would cut the
amplifier but still let the
signal straight through from the
aerial. At the moment, if I
switch it off the signal is lost
completely. It's too much of a
hassle to keep switching leads
and I have(really stupid)visions
that if I did, one day I should
suddenly see 'the most wonderful
program in the world' is just
starting on Channel 5 and I will
be in a panic trying to change
all the connections back! (my
video might also be in the
middle of recording the 'second
most wonderful program in the
world and would be interrupted).
I want to be ready just in case!


I can't remember if this has
been said in OUTLET before but
anyone who wants to retune their
video recorder themselves to av-
oid clashing with t CH5 (if it
has not happened yet it may due
in a few months) then...

[The following only applies if
your video is plugged in via the
aerial socket of your TV. If it
is connected via SCART or other
direct video link you don't need

controls to vary RF output:check
the manual!]

Look at the back of the video
recorder where the ouput lead to
the TV is plugged in. Nearby

thing distinctive that won't be
confused with a live program).
You could also use the video re-
corders built-in test card if it
has one and you know how to set
it up.

Slightly retune your TV on the
channel you play back the video
recorder until the picture just
disappears. Note the direction
you moved the tuning control.

Now, with a small screwdriver,
turn the tiny screw on the back
of the video slowly no more than
a quarter of turn one way until
the picture re-appears. If it
does not re-appear turn back and
try turning the other way.


You can repeat the whole thing
in slight increments, retuning
the TV slightly and then the
video to 'catch up' with it till
any picture distortion has gone.

The reason the waterboard turn

Dear Ron & Brian,

I have two separate models of INTERFACE 1.  According to the Microdrive formatting program INCREMAT, one has an old rom and the other has a new ROM. Can you please enlighten me as to the differences in the ROMS?

I believe there are different models of MULTIFACE 128. I have one, albeit quite elderly judg- ing by the instruction leaflet, which doesn't seem to like being in the same company as a DATEL +D interface.

Brian Cavers to Sam Quigg

Spectrum's fitted with Interface 1 shadow ROM Issue 2 will print 80 (after a reset) if you enter:

PRINT PEEK 23729

In Issue 2, the "t" channel out- put has been improved to support the TAB function and the comma control code (code 6 which tabs to column 16 then to the start of the next line). The leading space bug in Issue 1 has also been corrected.

There is the new system variable at 23729 mentioned above which you can POKE to alter line width when printing. (default is 80)

The CAT command and other 'read' routines should be faster in the Issue 2 because it doesn't waste time trying to read non-existent sectors.

One VERY important change is the memory check when accessing the drive. I used an Issue 1 Inter- face 1 while Ron had an Issue 2. As I recall, if there was less than around 700 bytes of memory free then the whole system would lock up and you had to reset. It drove me crazy at times, especi- ally if I had just spent half an hour writing a program and then it locked up when I went to SAVE it! This problem alone makes it well worth using an Issue 2!

A 'carriage return' (code 13) to start a new line is NOT sent when the "b" channel is CLOSEd with Issue 2 but was with Issue 1.

If BREAK was pressed during a CLOSE operation then it became impossible to remove the channel (from BASIC) with Issue 1. This bug has been corrected in Issue 2.

There are two new hook codes in Issue 2 for machine code progr- ammers but these don't affect BASIC. I have details if you want though.

Checks made by the FORMAT comm- and are direct OUT instructions in Issue 2 rather than using a channel - though I can't see it making any visible difference to the user.

There are other changes which, like the preceding, are probably not visible to the user but are simply more efficient routines used by the system etc.

I have fuller details should you need to know more about any of the differences. These are taken from the book, "Spectrum Shadow ROM Disassembly" by Gianluca Carri which you might spot at a Microfair if you are lucky!

Possibly your Multiface 128 is an earlier version that is not compatible with the +D. The only 128K Spectrum I have is the +3 but I do have the Lunter Z80 emulator on the PC. This can emulate a 128K Spectrum with +D and Multiface 128. I tried this and it successfully saved and reloaded a snapshot so clearly this version of Multiface IS compatible with the +D.

When you say, 'not compatible' do you mean the whole Spectrum crashes if both your Multiface and +D are connected - or that the Multiface will not operate? If, in fact, it does run and you can get the yellow menu bar at the bottom of the screen then...

If you select SAVE and enter a filename do you get options for tape, microdrive, Disciple and Opus? If you can get that far but there is no Disciple or +D option then I would say your particular Multiface is not compatible and may have been made even before the Disciple was launched.

However, if not compatible you might also get a hardware clash just by having the Multiface and +D connected to the Spectrum at the same time. If this happens then it's worth at least clean- ing the edge connector (switch off the power first!) just in case it simply a bad connection.

Short of buying a new Multiface I don't see what else you can do however, I do wonder what use a Multiface snapshot is on a +D when it has its own snapshot built in.

While testing a made a Multiface snapshot from the emulator on this current OUTLET disk of the HEAD OVER HEELS 128K game (on the +D version only). This can be loaded from BASIC with...

LOAD d*"HOHmf128" or LOAD P40

However, I am not sure what that will prove because I found it would reload into the emulator WITHOUT Multiface! Is that supp- osed to happen I wonder!

I know of THE LAST WORD but have not seen it I don't think. In OUTLET 42 there is an OUTLETTER from Andy Fleming who indicates he has it running on his +D. If you see this Andy, please write in and confirm!  I believe that Malcolm Perry has TLW too though uses OUTWRITE now on the SAM. If anyone else has any info on this please let us know or contact Sam Quigg direct (see his advert in OUTBOARD).

I could find nothing about conv- erting THE WRITER to print via the Spectrum 128K RS232 port but R.A. Roberts reported in OUTLET 71 that he had been helped by someone who got it working on a +D. Would that help?

If anyone else has any ideas on any of the subjects in this let- ter then please write!

Brian

To restore the normal Spectrum font (character set) after a new on has been displayed, use...

POKE 23670,0 POKE 23671,60

The rule is to POKE the address (usual two-byte format) of the font minus 256 and the standard font is in ROM at 60 * 256 + 0 which is 15616

To connect a +D to a +3 or +2A Spectrum buy a "FIXIT" off Brian Gaff (see later).

I am puzzled as to why you want TWO emulators but presumably a friend wants one too! Anyway,you can order them from Brian Gaff too (see later)

You are correct that the PC floppy drive will let you access your +D disks. This is a true emulation (though a bit slow) and means that you simply use EXACTLY THE SAME SYNTAX to load programs, eg, LOAD d1"name". It is exactly as if you had a Spec- trum with a +D attached!

Your disks may not be damaged.If you got a "No system file" error it just means there is no system file on that particular disk and you were entering "RUN" in a blank Spectrum which, with a +D, tries to first load the system file and then a BASIC program named "AUTO" followed by any six characters you like.

This is how you would normally use the +D.

1.Switch on the Spectrum or load the emulator if using a PC.

2.Put a disk in the drive with a system file on it. This file is named "+SYS" plus any six characters.

3. If the disk also has a BASIC program named "AUTO" plus any other six characters then it will also load and run but if not you just get an "OK".

4. There is no further need to load the system file ever again - even if you reset - unless (a) you switch off the machine and on again or... (b) the system gets corrupted (this sometimes happens with odd programs and you start getting odd disk errors).

5. Therefore, there is no need to have a system file on any other disk except one master and one or two backups disks.

6. To load further programs you use LOAD d1 "name" or LOAD Pn where "n" is the number shown in the CAT list. HOWEVER...

7. Some people PREFER to put the system file on all disks so they can then just enter RUN to load an AUTO file. I see little advantage in this as it is slower (because it has to keep loading TWO files!). I just always save my AUTO file as the first file on the disk and then I know I can always just enter LOAD P1. It is up to individual taste.

### Brian Cavers отвечает Sam Quigg

Спектрумы с теневым ПЗУ Interface 1 Issue 2 после сброса при вводе команды:

```basic
PRINT PEEK 23729
```

напечатают число 80.

В Issue 2 вывод через канал "t" был улучшен: добавлена поддержка функции TAB и управляющего кода запятой (код 6, который делает табуляцию на 16-ю колонку, а затем на начало следующей строки). Ошибка с лишним пробелом в начале строки из Issue 1 также была исправлена.

Появилась новая системная переменная по адресу 23729, упомянутая выше, которую можно изменять через POKE для настройки ширины строки при печати (по умолчанию 80).

Команда CAT и другие подпрограммы чтения в Issue 2 должны работать быстрее, так как система больше не тратит время на попытки прочесть несуществующие секторы.

Одно ОЧЕНЬ важное изменение — это проверка памяти при обращении к накопителю. Я использовал Interface 1 Issue 1, тогда как у Ron был Issue 2. Насколько я помню, если оставалось меньше примерно 700 байт свободной памяти, вся система намертво висла, и приходилось жать сброс. Временами это жутко бесило, особенно если ты только что потратил полчаса на написание программы, а она зависала при попытке сделать SAVE! Из-за одной этой проблемы уже стоит перейти на Issue 2!

Символ «возврата каретки» (код 13) для начала новой строки НЕ отправляется при закрытии (CLOSE) канала "b" в Issue 2, хотя отправлялся в Issue 1.

Если во время операции CLOSE была нажата клавиша BREAK, то в Issue 1 становилось невозможно удалить канал (из Бейсика). Этот баг исправлен в Issue 2.

Для программистов на машинном коде в Issue 2 добавлены два новых кода перехвата (hook codes), но на Бейсик они не влияют. Если нужно, у меня есть подробности.

Проверки, выполняемые командой FORMAT, в Issue 2 реализованы через прямые команды OUT, а не через канал — хотя сомневаюсь, что пользователь заметит какую-либо видимую разницу.

Есть и другие изменения, которые, как и предыдущие, скорее всего, незаметны пользователю, а представляют собой просто более эффективные системные подпрограммы и т. д.

У меня есть более подробная информация, если вам захочется узнать больше о различиях. Они взяты из книги «Spectrum Shadow ROM Disassembly» автора Gianluca Carri, которую вам, если повезет, удастся найти на какой-нибудь ярмарке Microfair!

Возможно, ваш Multiface 128 — это ранняя версия, не совместимая с +D. Единственный мой Spectrum 128K — это +3, но на ПК у меня есть эмулятор Lunter Z80. Он умеет эмулировать 128K Spectrum с интерфейсами +D и Multiface 128. Я проверил: он успешно сохранил и загрузил снимок памяти (snapshot), так что эта версия Multiface совершенно точно СОВМЕСТИМА с +D.

Говоря «не совместим», вы имеете в виду, что весь Spectrum зависает при одновременном подключении Multiface и +D — или что сам Multiface не срабатывает? Если на самом деле он запускается, и внизу экрана появляется желтая полоска меню, то...

Если вы выбираете SAVE и вводите имя файла, появляются ли варианты tape, microdrive, Disciple и Opus? Если до этого шага доходит, но опций Disciple или +D нет, то я бы сказал, что конкретно ваша версия Multiface несовместима и, возможно, была выпущена еще до появления Disciple.

Впрочем, в случае несовместимости может возникать и аппаратный конфликт просто от одновременного подключения Multiface и +D к Спектруму. Если дело в этом, стоит хотя бы почистить краевой разъем (сначала выключив питание!), на случай если это просто плохой контакт.

Если не покупать новый Multiface, я не знаю, что еще можно сделать, однако я вообще сомневаюсь в полезности снэпшотов Multiface на +D, когда у самого +D есть встроенная функция сохранения слепков.

Мое начинание YTC — куда более простая (и безопасная) альтернатива для меня и нескольких близких друзей, которые занимаются электроникой ради удовольствия, а не как профессией, отбрасывая тем самым большую часть сложной физики. Электроны для души тоже имеют право на жизнь.

Я усердно работал над своим проектом YTC с момента получения последнего ежеквартального бюллетеня BAEC в январе этого года, полагая, что всё идёт хорошо, но [перспектива остаться] без OUTLET определённо ставит мне палки в колёса.

А, впрочем, неважно. Совершенно очевидно, что пользователей +D много, и поэтому они заслуживают самого пристального внимания со стороны OUTLET.

5.25" дискеты скоро иссякнут; то же самое произойдёт и с 3.5" DD. Насколько мне известно, производство DD-дисководов по всему миру уже прекращено в пользу более поздних HD. Но ведь и эти 1.44mb дисководы скоро повторят ту же судьбу в пользу более поздних 2mb и гигабайтных накопителей?

В свете всего этого я уже запасся 3.5" DD-дисководами и дискетами DD. Если вы получили ошибку «No system file», это просто означает, что на данном конкретном диске нет системного файла, а вы ввели «RUN» на чистом Spectrum, который в случае с +D сначала пытается загрузить системный файл, а затем программу на BASIC с именем «AUTO», за которым следуют любые шесть символов по вашему выбору.

Вот как обычно следует работать с +D:

1. Включите Spectrum или загрузите эмулятор, если используете PC.
2. Вставьте в дисковод дискету с системным файлом. Этот файл называется «+SYS» плюс любые шесть символов.
3. Если на диске также есть программа на BASIC с именем «AUTO» плюс любые другие шесть символов, то она загрузится и запустится автоматически, а если нет — вы просто получите сообщение «OK».

4. Больше нет никакой необходимости загружать системный файл снова — даже при сбросе (reset) — если только (a) вы не выключите компьютер и не включите его снова или... (b) система не повредится (такое иногда случается со странными программами, и вы начинаете получать странные дисковые ошибки).

5. Следовательно, нет никакой необходимости держать системный файл на каком-либо другом диске, кроме одного мастер-диска и одной-двух резервных копий.
